script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for August 11. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
A cheetah moves at 70 mph.  Light moves at 670 million mph.  Speed is how much distance you cover in how much time.

Speed equals distance divided by time. To go faster, cover more ground—or do it in less time. Both levers work. Sometimes efficiency gains are easier than effort increases. Speed is how fast; velocity includes direction.  You can be moving fast but in the wrong direction—high speed, wrong velocity.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Speed isn't just moving fast—it's the relationship between distance and time.  Check your direction, find sustainable pace, and optimize for speed that lasts.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Speed Check - Progress Per Time.

Here's your activity: Pick a goal. How much progress have you made in the last month? Is that speed sufficient to reach your goal in your timeframe? Could you go faster by working differently (not just harder)? Speed is about efficiency, not just effort. This helps you evaluate progress efficiency.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about how fast things go can be applied to speed check - progress per time. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
